extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and legal/compliance staff at recipients
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for educational institution recipients on conducting Title IX grievance procedures (investigations, evidence access, privacy, and impartiality) consistent with final regulations. Focused on operationalizing §§106.45 and related provisions for K-12 and postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of irrelevant information while complying with §106.45/§106.46
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may redact information that is not relevant to the allegations of sex discrimination; however, a recipient must, when redacting information, ensure that the recipient is fully complying with its obligations under §106.45, and if applicable §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When redacting, ensure compliance with privacy protections and duties to prevent unauthorized disclosures (see §§106.45(b)(5), 106.45(f)(4)(iii), 106.46(e)(6)). See related discussions of §§106.6(e), 106.45(b)(5) and (f)(4), and 106.46(e)(6) for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA exception for school officials with legitimate educational interest
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA permits a recipient to disclose personally identifiable information from a student's education record without prior written consent if the disclosure is to a school official who has been determined to have a legitimate educational interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the criteria set forth in the educational agency's or institution's annual notification of FERPA rights. See 20 U.S.C. 1232g(b)(1)(A); 34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii), 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigations (§106.45(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of complaints as the foundation for equitable adjudications and equitable treatment of complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations contain numerous procedural requirements across stages of investigation and resolution to support fair outcomes. The Department will offer technical assistance and guidance as appropriate. No additional paragraph on impartiality was added because §106.45(f) already requires impartial investigations; §106.45(b)(1) also requires equitable treatment of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient bears burden to conduct investigation (§106.45(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient, and not the parties, bears the burden to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to make a determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department replaced legalistic phrases with the accessible phrase 'burden ... to conduct an investigation,' but the meaning is the same. Recipients may not shift the burden to respondents to prove consent or to complainants to prove absence of consent. FERPA does not relieve a recipient of this obligation. See prior discussion (85 FR 30125) and related sections (§§106.6(e), 106.45(e), (f)(4), 106.46(e)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present fact witnesses and relevant, not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.45(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an equal opportunity for the parties to present fact witnesses and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance is defined in §106.2. Evidence that is 'impermissible' is described by §106.45(b)(7) and must be excluded regardless of relevance. Recipients retain discretion to allow expert witnesses (subject-matter-specific rules for student postsecondary cases are in §106.46(e)(4)). Character evidence is not categorically allowed or disallowed; it must meet the relevance standard. Recipients must objectively evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence per §106.45(b)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators must review all gathered evidence for relevance and impermissibility (§106.45(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must review all evidence gathered throughout the investigation and assess that evidence for relevance and impermissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevance determinations may be made throughout the investigation, but recipients remain responsible for assessing relevance in light of all evidence gathered and may need to revisit earlier relevance exclusions to avoid inadvertently excluding relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access relevant evidence or accurate description (§106.45(f)(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide each party with an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant to the allegations of sex discrimination and not otherwise impermissible, either by (a) providing access to the underlying evidence ('evidence option') or (b) providing an accurate description of such evidence ('description option'). If the recipient initially chooses the description option and then any party requests access to the evidence, the recipient must provide access to the underlying relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description must be 'accurate'—it must fairly summarize the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence and be sufficient to provide the parties with a reasonable opportunity to respond, prepare arguments, contest relevance, and present additional evidence. Recipients cannot give unequal access (one party access to underlying evidence while another receives only a description). The equal opportunity requirement extends to mode of delivery, though auxiliary aids or language assistance may be provided to individual parties as needed to ensure effective communication. Recipients have discretion on form (oral or written) but must document oral descriptions in some manner to comply with §106.8(f)(1) (e.g., audio recording). Recipients may tailor approach based on ages of parties, severity, volume of evidence, and case-specific factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description option may be used but must be sufficient and parties may request underlying evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient choosing the description option may provide the description orally or in writing and is not required to provide a written investigative report under §106.45(f)(4); however, the description must be accurate and sufficient, and the parties have the right to request and receive access to the underlying evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike §106.46(e)(6) (which addresses written investigative reports for postsecondary student sex-based harassment), §106.45(f)(4) contemplates that a written investigative report may not be necessary or appropriate for complaints covered by §106.45. Recipients may nonetheless provide a written report if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable opportunity to respond to the evidence or description (§106.45(f)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must give the parties a reasonable opportunity to respond to the evidence or to the accurate description of the evidence; the opportunity must be meaningful so parties can respond effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is 'reasonable' depends on the nature and volume of evidence; the Department declines to provide examples. The opportunity to respond will generally take place at the end of the investigation but recipients may allow responses at other points in the investigation. Apply Goss (notice and meaningful opportunity to be heard) principles where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosures (§106.45(f)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize chilling effects, retaliation, harassment, and other harms, recipients must take reasonable steps to prevent and address parties' unauthorized disclosure of information provided under §106.45(f)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department does not prescribe specific steps; what is reasonable will vary by circumstances. Steps may range from informing parties of expectations and consequences to implementing technological measures (software restrictions) that limit further distribution. Consider privacy protections required by §106.45(f)(4)(iii) when providing access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must articulate consistent principles for choosing description vs evidence (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for determining when the recipient will initially provide a description of the evidence or access to the underlying evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should include in their procedures the criteria they will use (e.g., age of parties, severity of alleged conduct) so that initial choices are consistent and transparent. This helps address due process concerns and collective bargaining considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity requirement does not mandate identical treatment where accessibility differs
rubrics_metrics.description: An equal opportunity to access the evidence requires providing the same description or same access to the underlying evidence to all parties, but does not require identical treatment in every respect; recipients may need to provide auxiliary aids/services or language assistance to individual parties to ensure effective communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing auxiliary aids (e.g., format changes, interpreters) to one party to ensure effective communication is consistent with equal opportunity even if the other party does not require the same aids. Similarly, modes of delivery may differ for accessibility reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disclosure of complainant's sexual interests/prior sexual conduct except narrow exceptions (§106.45(b)(7)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations prohibit a recipient from disclosing evidence of the complainant's sexual interests and prior sexual conduct, except as narrowly permitted by §106.45(b)(7)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition of 'relevant' was expanded, but this prohibition is an explicit exception to disclosure; see the discussion of §106.2 and §106.45(b)(7)(iii) for the limited circumstances in which such information may be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmakers must objectively evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker is required to evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for its persuasiveness when making determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation works with the equal-opportunity and relevance requirements to ensure fair evaluation; corroboration is permissive (may be considered) but not required to reach a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators/Title IX personnel must not have conflicts of interest or bias (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific requirement supporting impartial investigations and determinations; recipients should ensure assignment practices and trainings address conflicts and bias.
